display.title: Nanas the Butcher: A Place in Gan Eden for Honoring Parents
display.summary_short: A great sage dreams that his place in Gan Eden will be next to Nanas the butcher, and sets out to discover what makes this simple man so special.
display.summary_long: A Mitzvah Time story about kibbud av va'em from the Tzivos Hashem radio show. The great tzaddik Rabbi Yehoshua dreams that he will sit beside Nanas the butcher in Gan Eden. Puzzled, he recalls his lifetime of awe of Heaven, Torah study and mitzvos, his tzitzis and tefillin and his eighty students, and sends his students to find this Nanas. The townspeople say he is just a simple man, and Nanas himself cannot believe that the great rabbi is asking for him. So Rabbi Yehoshua goes himself, and Nanas falls at his feet. Asked what he does all day, Nanas explains that he is a plain butcher who cares for his very old and helpless father and mother, dressing, washing and feeding them every day. Rabbi Yehoshua kisses him and says how fortunate he is to share Nanas's place in Gan Eden.
display.lesson: Caring for your parents with devotion is so great that a simple man can earn the same place in Gan Eden as a great sage.

date.note: Cut from episode 162, broadcast on the eve of Tu B'Shvat 5745 (Tue 1985-02-05).
